summary.title: Making A Website With Haskell
summary.one_liner: Learn how to build, template, persist, and deploy a simple Haskell web app using Scotty, blaze-html, and Persistent, with Heroku deployment steps (the post is marked outdated).
takeaways: Set up an isolated Haskell project with a Cabal sandbox and a .cabal file listing dependencies
Write Scotty routes for GET/POST/PUT/DELETE, params, headers, and JSON/text/HTML responses
Render HTML views with blaze-html and serve static files via WAI middleware
Define Persistent models and run SQLite or PostgreSQL queries, then deploy to Heroku with a buildpack and Procfile
summary.summary: This tutorial walks through building a small Haskell website with Scotty (a Sinatra-like framework on Warp), blaze-html for templates, and Persistent for database access. It covers project setup with a Cabal sandbox, a hello-world app, routing, headers, content types, logging, static files, a SQLite model, and deploying to Heroku with a PostgreSQL switch. It also briefly covers testing with wai-test and lists missing features like cookies and asset aggregation. The page is explicitly marked as old and out of date, with dependency versions pinned to 2013-2014 era packages.
